title: Tips & best practices
intro: Improvement principles grouped by the source each set comes from. Each source has its own page with all of its tips (no cap) and searchable tags; open the hub to filter across every source at once. Tips are paraphrased principles in the spirit of each creator — not verbatim quotes.

sources.name: kiritastrich
sources.blurb: Russian-language strategy channel — timings, economy math, patch analysis (translated here).

tips.text: On water/hybrid maps Fast Castle is the whole game — but since Docks now fire 0 arrows in the Dark Age you can't shelter fishing ships under the Dock, so play Feudal (Galleys / Fire Ships) to defend them.
Reason in gathering rates, not totals: rate × time decides timings, so chase the fastest food (boar, deer, shore fish) before slow berries.
On resource-rich starts (2+ boar, 8 sheep, 3-4 deer), a Fast-Castle → scouts + scorpions + monks opener snowballs hard.
Fish traps are the most wood-efficient food — 100 wood beats a 60-wood farm and skips all three Mill farm upgrades; if you win the water, keep making fishing ships past ~12.
In draft, civilization reflects a gameplan: ban a player's comfort start to tilt them, and scout their first minutes to disrupt their build.
Eat food sources in speed order — boar and shore fish first, sheep next, berries last — so your fastest gatherers are never stuck on the slowest source.
A clean no-idle Fast Castle (e.g. a 17+2 Mongols build clicking Castle around 18 pop) converts an eco bonus into a timing the opponent has to answer.
Full-feudal aggression civs (Incas, Mapuche, Tupi, Muisca) must wall: their plan wins by early pressure, so closing the map denies the opponent's faster age-up.

Continuous unique-unit production from a Castle or Monastery drains ~168 food/min — about 8 unbowed farms — so line up that many farms before committing to UU spam; Monastery-UU + rams can out-push Castle-UU.
One-trick civ/build abusers rarely beat prepared tournament opponents — only near-perfect execution (e.g. Hoang) sustains it; broaden your pool rather than leaning on a single abuse build.

Goths are an infantry-rush civ, yet their navy is nearly complete — the full ship line plus Careening and Shipwright, missing only Dry Dock — though with no economy or water bonuses behind it, it's a hybrid-map flex rather than a real gameplan.

sources.name: Spirit of the Law
sources.blurb: Data-driven AoE2 analysis — the numbers behind why things work.

tips.text: Never let the Town Center idle — constant villager production is the single biggest skill in the game.
Counter-composition wins: Skirmishers into Archers, Pikemen into Knights, Mangonels into massed Archers. Build the counter, not a mirror.
Double-Bit Axe is the best-return Feudal economy upgrade; grab it the instant you click Feudal, and keep lumber/farm upgrades rolling through Castle.
Wall when you boom or fall behind — walls deny raids and buy the time a slower plan needs.
Don't float resources: a bank is army and upgrades you didn't make. If wood climbs, spend it on farms or military.
Bonus-damage classes matter more than raw attack — read what your unit counters and aim it at the right target.
Cheap-tech civs (Chinese, Byzantines) compound with game length — every discounted technology is resources freed for another unit or upgrade.
Siege is the late-game answer to massed ranged/infantry: Onagers and Mangonels force fights you would lose in a straight shoot-out.
A strong general economy bonus is the most reliable foundation — it is flexible, forgives mistakes, and defines almost every recent top civ.
Fishing ships are villagers that cost wood, not food — on water maps a strong navy multiplies your economy and snowballs.

sources.name: Hera
sources.blurb: Top pro player — fundamentals, decision-making, and macro.

tips.text: Scout constantly — knowing the opponent's strategy, resources and army is the edge that wins even games.
Macro before micro: keep villagers and military producing before you micro a single fight; production wins the war.
Add Town Centers in Castle Age and keep booming — villager count decides the late game.
Defend your economy first; a clean home base (houses ahead, drop-offs tight) survives aggression and out-scales it.
Control the map's key resources and relics — map control compounds into an economy lead.
Never stop making villagers and army — floating the resources to queue both is where lower-Elo players bleed.
Adapt your army to what you scouted: switch compositions before you're hard-countered, not after.
Pre-wall likely raid paths while you macro — cheap prevention beats expensive repair.

sources.name: CyberDabVinc
sources.blurb: Defensive and boom-focused coaching — reliable plans for climbing the ladder.

tips.text: Wall + boom is the most reliable plan for newer players: walls let you macro in peace and reach a power spike.
Hit your build-order timings — click Feudal/Castle at the right villager count so your spike lands on schedule.
Never fight a bad matchup: retreat, re-tech to the counter, and re-engage on your terms.
Use Towers and Castles to lock down hills, relics and forward resources — stone is map control.
Keep base discipline: houses ahead of the pop cap, drop-off buildings tight to resources, zero TC idle time.
Don't over-commit to one fight — disengage, heal/regroup, and trade efficiently across the whole game.
A forward Castle with a ram or unique-unit flood is a clean way to close out a lead you've boomed.
Spend, don't hoard: every 100 idle wood is a farm or military unit you're behind on.
